channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy won’t make the 53-man roster.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

McCarthy left preseason Week 2 with an ankle injury and returned to practice before ultimately missing preseason Week 3 altogether. According to Lewis, that only added to the murkiness about McCarthy’s 2026 status. All signs point to Carson Wentz as the QB2 after he started Friday’s game against the Broncos. Lewis adds that “McCarthy’s comfort (or lack thereof) with being QB3 could dictate his future in Minnesota” and projects that the Vikings won’t carry him on the 53-man roster to begin the regular season. The 10th overall pick in the draft only two years ago, McCarthy’s path to being a reclamation project for another organization could arrive sooner than anyone thought. Stay tuned.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Bills released WR Mecole Hardman.
item.description:
Mecole Hardman

Hardman’s release was first reported by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. A seven-year NFL veteran, Hardman spent most of his career with the Chiefs, where he helped Kansas City win three Super Bowls. Last year he appeared in only two games with the Bills and dropped passes were an issue in training camp and preseason this year. Hardman will head to the open market where he could be a fit for another team looking for wide receiver depth.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles told reporters “hopefully” WR Emeka Egbuka (toe) is ready for Week 1.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka continues to deal with a minor toe injury. Bowles said in recent weeks that he was optimistic about Egbuka’s status, but also wasn’t sure if he’d be available for Week 1. Now he’s hopeful that the 23-year-old wide receiver will be available. The Buccaneers don’t seem too concerned about the injury at this point, making Egbuka a solid WR2 in fantasy drafts.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Giants acquired DL C.J. Okoye from the Ravens in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
item.description:
C.J. Okoye NYG Defensive Lineman

The news was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. The draft pick going to the Ravens is a 2028 seventh-round pick. Okoye reunites with Giants HC John Harbaugh after playing under him in Baltimore in 2025. A former UDFA from Nigeria, Okoye figures to bolster the Giants interior defensive line depth as a rotational player.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Cyrus Allen caught 1-of-2 targets for 12 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

The Chiefs let most of their starters take the field in this game and Allen wasn’t among them. He didn’t see a snap until after Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Tyquan Thornton had all left the contest. His first target didn’t come until the third quarter, and it was a drop on a high throw. The rookie rebounded with a 12-yard gain for a first down on the very next play. After playing well into the second half of the team’s final preseason game, Allen is, at best, the Chiefs’ WR4 entering the season. Despite the strong training camp, he shouldn’t be in starting fantasy lineups for Week 1.

item.title: Odell Beckham caught 3-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Giants’ preseason game against the Jets.
item.description:
Odell Beckham NYG Wide Receiver

Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields rested. Malik Nabers, still recovering from his 2025 ACL tear, was held out. Beckham drew the start along with the rest of the second-string offense. His stat line was impressive and it nearly went stratospheric when he burned the Jets’ secondary for a would-be 70-yard touchdown. Jameis Winston overthrew the pass and Beckham was unable to haul it in despite laying out for the catch. Per the eye test, Beckham still has something in the tank, even if that something is likely just good enough for a depth role. He isn’t a lock to make the Giants’ roster, but this preseason showing certainly helped.

item.title: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker rushed five times for 15 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

Tucker and RB Josh Williams competed for the Buccaneers’ No. 3 running back job all night. Tucker got the start, touching the ball on three of the first four plays. Unfortunately, the drive ultimately ended in a punt, as did almost all of the others. It was an unproductive night for the Buccaneers’ offense. Williams entered the game on the second drive, and the two players continued to rotate in and out thereafter. Williams rushed eight times for 21 yards. Tucker caught one pass for minus-one yard as well. Neither player really separated from the other in the box score. The team must now choose between the trusted, higher-priced veteran, Tucker, and the more affordable second-year player, Williams. If Tucker is released, it could allow “1A” RB Bucky Irving to hoard short-yardage and goal-line work, which would significantly boost his fantasy-scoring outlook.

item.title: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Emmett Johnson KC Running Back

Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

item.title: Saints WR Bryce Lance caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Bryce Lance NO Wide Receiver

Lance could have the inside track for the Saints’ short-term No. 3 wide receiver job with WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) sidelined, though WR Barion Brown will almost assuredly make the roster as a receiver and returner. Lance nearly added a decent, leaping downfield gain to his box score, but QB Spencer Rattler’s pass grazed off his fingertips along the sideline. Brown was not involved as a receiver today, but rushed twice for 19 yards and one touchdown, including an eight-yard jet sweep that got him into the end zone. He also returned one punt for four yards.

item.title: Carson Wentz completed 3-of-4 passes for 15 yards in the Vikings’ preseason game against the Broncos.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

Wentz started this game and was on the field for two drives, both of which resulted in punts. J.J. McCarthy missed this game with an ankle issue and was already fighting for the backup job. The missed practice time and recurring injury issues likely have him behind Wentz on the depth chart when Week 1 comes around. The hope for Vikings fans is that Murray is a capable distributor of the football and neither Wentz nor McCarthy sees the field this year.

item.title: Marvin Mims (foot) is questionable to return in the Broncos’ preseason game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

The questionable designation is a formality. The teams will not throw Mims back into this game after he left with a foot issue in the first half. Mims’ role as a receiver declined last year, but he remains one of the league’s best returners. Sean Payton would need to figure out a plan for both kick and punt return duties.

Source: Troy Renck

item.title: Cowboys RB Malik Davis was held out with the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Saints.
item.description:
Malik Davis DAL Running Back

Davis appears to have secured a roster spot, but we won’t know for sure until Sunday. The broadcast initially referred to him as the starter, but it was instead RB Phil Mafah who took the field. Mafah dominated backfield touches throughout the first half, repeatedly running into Saints defenders on runs up the middle. He was spelled by RB Israel Abanikanda. Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue does not seem to be playing this evening. Last Sunday, The Athletic’s Jon Machota predicted Blue would seize the No. 2 running back job from Davis in-season.

item.title: Giants announced RB Tyrone Tracy was evaluated for concussion, but was cleared.
item.description:
Tyrone Tracy NYG Running Back

Tracy left Friday’s preseason game against the Jets with an apparent injury in the second quarter. The Giants announced Tracy was evaluated for a concussion, but was able to clear concussion protocol. Before leaving the game, Tracy had 37 yards and a touchdown on four carries. He doesn’t carry much standalone fantasy value in a crowded Giants backfield that also includes Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris and Devin Singletary.

Source: Ralph Vacchiano

item.title: Giants RB Najee Harris rushed 11 times for 39 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Jets, adding one reception for 20 yards.
item.description:
Najee Harris NYG Running Back

Harris saw his first game action since he suffered a torn Achilles last year. The 28-year-old running back had 39 yards on 11 carries and his longest run was for nine yards. Harris added a 20-yard reception, giving him 59 scrimmage yards on 12 opportunities. Harris was brought in to be a “significant contributor” to the Giants, according to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan. He looked the part in Friday’s preseason finale against the Jets.

item.title: Eagles WR Makai Lemon caught 3-of-5 targets for three yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Makai Lemon PHI Wide Receiver

Lemon had a rough night, but tonight’s outcome does not make him any less of a top-tier prospect. The first-round rookie was sidelined by a recurring hamstring injury for much of the spring and summer, so a rusty first showing is understandable. Lemon took the blame, on the field, for QB Tanner McKee’s interception, although it is fair to note that McKee’s pass arrived late. Lemon had broken inward, off his stem, and an open window was available to the Eagles’ backup quarterback. Unfortunately, Lemon was forced to slow down and leap for the pass, accidentally batting it backward as he attempted to high-point it. Bengals CB Tacario Davis snagged it and that was that. Davis also broke up a pass intended for Lemon on a corner route 20 yards downfield earlier in the game. He had a good night. Lemon may need to ramp up for another couple of weeks, but he remains a smart draft pick in 12-team leagues. Lemon later went back into the game to field a punt, but went nowhere with it.

item.title: Bengals WR Dohnte Meyers caught 3-of-3 targets for 51 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Dohnte Meyers CIN Wide Receiver

Meyers seemingly has the No. 4 wide receiver job locked up. On the first drive, he hauled in three passes. He bagged a nine-yard pass on an in-breaking route from the slot on the first, a 17-yard pass via a corner route from the slot and a 25-yard gain on the following play. The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. labeled Meyers a “roster lock,” saying at first a special teams returner role seemed to be Meyers’ ticket to a roster spot, but “the consistency of his playmaking at every turn of camp and the preseason made him undeniable.” He ran with the first-team offense in practice this week, and Bengals wide receivers coach Troy Walters said, “he can play all three positions.” File Meyers’ name away for down the road.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy left preseason Week 3’s game against the Jets with an injury.
item.description:
Tyrone Tracy NYG Running Back

Tracy went down after an eight-yard run late in the second quarter. After he was on the ground for a while, Tracy headed to the locker room with a trainer. While the nature of his injury remains unclear, Tracy was an effective runner against the Jets with 37 yards and a touchdown on four carries.

item.title: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports that Bengals WR Colbie Young is still “picking up the details of the complicated offense.”
item.description:
Colbie Young CIN Wide Receiver

Per Dehner, Young has “made as many highlight catches as anyone, validating the Bengals’ fourth-round pick.” He believes “the seeds of a bright future were planted” for Young this summer. That said, Young is still developing and is likely to start the season as the Bengals’ No. 5 wide receiver.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Falcons TE Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-3 targets for 59 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Kyle Pitts ATL Tight End

Pitts ripped off multiple double-digit gains, moved well and looked tough to bring down. He delivered a 37-yard catch on the Falcons’ first drive, securing the pass on a quick out route from bunch formation before taking off down the right sideline. He later had a 16-yard gain on a sort crossing route, where he again chewed up yards after the catch. Pitts is a mid-tier TE1 entering the year.

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa completed 7-of-8 passes for 95 yards and lost one fumble in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

It was a rough day for Tagovailoa. The Falcons quarterback was greeted by boos in his former home stadium this evening. He maintained his relatively low level of play, throwing short and, at one point, fumbling a snap, which was recovered by a Dolphins defender. It was not his worst showing, but it is unlikely to earn him the starting job either.

item.title: Dolphins WR Chris Bell caught 2-of-5 targets for 22 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell played in the preseason for the first time this evening. He got involved early and looked good. He snagged a four-yard catch on the first play from scrimmage and hauled in an 18-yarder on the next drive by finding the soft spot in the Falcons’ zone coverage on a post route. Bell got shaken up by a hard hit while unsuccessfully attempting to bring in another pass, but he remained on the field and came back out for the next drive as well. Bell’s return from an ACL tear seems to be going well, and the Dolphins’ wide receiver depth chart has open roles. Unsurprisingly, Bell said after the game that he will be ready to go for Week 1. He should be targeted as a last-round pick in 12-team fantasy drafts.

item.title: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas was held out with the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas has seemingly secured a starting role in his rookie season. The big-bodied downfield wide receiver looked good in the first preseason game and played just three snaps in the second one. The Dolphins are expected to field a run-heavy offense, but Douglas could warrant FLEX treatment before long. He should be targeted late in drafts.

item.title: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen’s “ability to be a quality route runner should make him one of the Chiefs’ top answers” against man coverage.
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

Taylor stops short of declaring Allen a starter in three-wide receiver sets, so he is likely still stuck in the No. 4 wide receiver spot. The fifth-round rookie has at least carved out a role for himself, and Taylor dubs him “the biggest winner in camp.” Allen is a worthwhile late-round pick at this time.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy (ankle) won’t play in preseason Week 3 against the Broncos, reports Alec Lewis of the Athletic.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

The Vikings hoped that McCarthy’s ankle injury would heal, but ultimately the 23-year-old quarterback isn’t ready to play. The injury is considered minor and McCarthy is day-to-day, according to Lewis. While minor, McCarthy’s injury has cost him valuable reps as he now finds himself battling Carson Wentz for the QB2 job.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. said he “wouldn’t be surprised if the Bengals double last year’s” number of runs from under center on early downs.
item.description:
Chase Brown CIN Running Back

Dehner has been covering the Bengals’ intent to increase the number of plays run from under center all summer. Last season, “the Bengals ran from under center 120 times on early downs. The league average was 210.” Per Dehner, it has become clear “over the weeks that the under-center offense would not be going away.” The Bengals are committed to changing their ways in pursuit of more explosive gains. Starting RB Chase Brown is a locked-in RB1.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Raiders QB Kirk Cousins is expected to be named the starter eventually.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

Appearing on NFL Live Friday afternoon, Fowler said that people inside the Raiders’ building and around the league still expect Cousins to be named the starter. Raiders HC Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback Friday morning. Following the loss of Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, Kubiak said rookie Fernando Mendoza needs another three preseason games before going as far as mentioning that Mendoza’s practice reps will decline once the regular season begins. While Kubiak continues to drag his feet when it comes to the official announcement, all signs still point to Cousins being named the starter at some point eventually.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.description:
Jaheim Bell

The Steelers also waived CB Jaylon Guilbeau, S Jack Henderson, DB Brandon Hill, DB Tamon Lynum, DB Daryl Porter, OL Gregory Crippen, RB Alex Tecza, WR Jakobie Keeney-James and WR Isaiah Winstead. The Steelers released WR Cornell Powell

item.title: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports, “any doubt about” Bengals DT Dexter Lawrence’s “condition and impact evaporated from the first 11-on-11 session of camp.”
item.description:
Dexter Lawrence CIN Defensive Tackle

The Bengals sent the No. 10 overall pick in this year’s draft to acquire the disgruntled former Giant. Per Dehner, Bears coach Ben Johnson described him as “a menace” in joint practices, and QB Caleb Williams referred to him as “an All-Pro guy” and a “force to be reckoned with.” It sounds like things are panning out for Lawrence. Whether he can spark a defensive turnaround in Cincinnati remains to be seen, but the 28-year-old defensive tackle could pose problems this season.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes WR Josh Cameron would be the fill-in starter if a Jaguars starting wide receiver misses time.

Josh Cameron

item.title: Titans hosted free agent S Will Harris for a visit on Friday.
item.description:
Will Harris

A fibula injury sidelined Harris for Weeks 4-12 last season. He totaled two pass breakups, 27 tackles and one quarterback pressure while active.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Browns released TE Jack Stoll.
item.description:
Jack Stoll

The Browns also released CB Tre Avery, CB Tyler Hall and OT Tyre Phillips. The Browns waived TE Drew Biber, OT Jeremiah Byers, P Nik Constantinou, S Christopher Edmonds, CB Nate Evans, DT Coziah Izzard, DT Patrick Jenkins, CB Jeremiah McClendon, T Izavion Miller, DE Jamil Muhammad, WR Ben Patterson and TE Jermaine Terry II.

Source: Cleveland Browns

item.title: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden said “it looks like” Raiders RB Mike Washington “has changed the staff’s perspective of the running back room.”
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the backfield’s status with Washington coming off top-tier preseason play while RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) rehabs his recent injury. Kubiak said he is “not making any promises on percentages of play time,” but he thinks both backs “will prepare to play a lot of football and as these games unfold, you react to the game.” McFadden used the term “1-2 punch” to sum up Kubiak’s potential running back usage. McFadden also notes that “in May, Kubiak talked about using Jeanty as a bell cow running back,” and reports of that nature continued rolling in through early August. Washington has wowed as of late, though, and may be able to generate FLEX-worthy stat lines alongside Jeanty this season.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Pewter Report’s Matt Matera reports that the Buccaneers’ Friday night preseason game against the Jaguars could determine who wins the RB3 role.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

Second-year Buccaneers RB Josh Williams has played extensively, and even ahead of RB Sean Tucker, in the preseason thus far. Coach Todd Bowles has avoided answering questions about Tucker’s status directly, instead saying Williams is playing well and the staff wanted to see Williams play against better defenders early in preseason games. While this might not seem like a big deal, it could be for RB Bucky Irving. Tucker has been discussed as the team’s short-yardage and goal-line specialist this season. He is also set to make the second-highest salary in the backfield this year, yet none of it is guaranteed. Releasing him would save the team cash and potentially free up red zone duties for Irving to reclaim. Keep an eye on this position battle tonight.

Source: Pewter Report

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter has taken reps “almost exclusively at cornerback” for the last two weeks.
item.description:
Travis Hunter

Shipley estimates that Hunter has logged fewer than 10 reps at wide receiver in team drills during that span. Shipley said, “it seems like” the Jaguars are treating Hunter like their CB1. He also still thinks “there will be games where he logs 50 percent of the offensive snaps,” though. The biggest takeaway is that Hunter has an extremely wide range of potential outcomes, and he cannot be counted on to be FLEX-viable at this time.

Source: Prowler Podcast

item.title: Browns waived EDGE Jamil Muhammad.
item.description:
Jamil Muhammad

The Browns also waived CB Jeremiah McClendon. NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson believes Muhammad had a nice showing in training camp, and McClendon had strong showings in preseason games. Perhaps they will land elsewhere in the NFL.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson “is not believed” to have suffered a concussion.
item.description:
Wan'Dale Robinson TEN Wide Receiver

This is good to hear. New Titans OC Brian Daboll brought Robinson with him from the Giants to serve as a reliable go-to option for QB Cam Ward, particularly on third down. Robinson has a chance to lead the Titans in targets this season, though questions about the offense’s overall effectiveness could keep him stuck in FLEX spots, rather than the WR3 tier.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton is still working his way back from an undisclosed injury.
item.description:
Dont'e Thornton LV Wide Receiver

We still don’t know what Thornton is dealing with, but the second-year receiver hasn’t practiced since August 7th. Kubiak said earlier this month that he expected Thornton to return sometime during the preseason, but that didn’t come to fruition. Even if he’s able to make it back on the practice field ahead of Week 1, Thornton is unlikely to make any major contributions to the offense at this time.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty is “still on the mend” as he recovers from his ankle injury.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Funny enough, it’s the same line Kubiak provided to reporters on Tuesday when asked about the health of his RB1. Kubiak did say that the Raiders were “counting on (Jeanty)” for Week 1, but that’s hardly a sign that the Raiders expect him to suit up. With teams not being required to release official injury reports until the week leading up to the first game of the season, it’s possible that we won’t have a clear answer regarding Jeanty and his availability until the Raiders begin preparing for Week 1’s game against the Dolphins. In the event Jeanty can’t go, rookie Mike Washington is expected to see a substantial role after a solid preseason in which he rushed 23 times for 168 yards while averaging an impressive 7.3 YPC. Washington is worth a draft pick in all formats right now, especially with Jeanty’s status up in the air.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Colts WR Alec Pierce said “Week 1 is the goal” after being activated from the active/PUP list on Thursday.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce said the Colts have been doing a good job of preparing him to play even while sidelined, and with 16 days to go before the Colts host the Ravens in Week 1, it’s not inconceivable that he could be ready in time for the season opener. The Colts will continue to ramp Pierce up in the coming weeks, making his status one to monitor, especially when teams begin releasing official injury reports ahead of game day. If he is able to play, fantasy managers should view Pierce as anything more than a boom/bust WR3 until we see how he looks on the field.

Source: ProFootballTalk on NBCSports.com

item.title: ESPN’s Jeff Legwold believes Broncos RB Jonah Coleman “will get plenty of work” this season.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Legwold writes that the fourth-round rookie is “squarely in the backfield rotation” for the Broncos. Coleman possesses a three-down skill set that could open the door for him to eat into both J.K. Dobbins’ and RJ Harvey’s roles, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to put him in their lineups at this time. Dobbins is still considered the favorite to lead the Broncos in early-down touches to start the season, with most of Harvey’s looks coming on third down and in passing situations. That said, Coleman is one of the higher upside stashes at his position who could prove to have top-24 upside or better at some point this season.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler says he is expecting to see Najee Harris in the Giants’ final preseason game against the Jets.
item.description:
Najee Harris NYG Running Back

This will be the first look we get at Harris since he suffered a torn Achilles in Week 3 last season. The 28-year-old vet signed a deal with the Giants less than two weeks ago, but could end up being a “significant contributor” to the Giants’ backfield, per ESPN’s Jordan Raanan. Whether or not Harris has any fantasy value as a standalone option with Cam Skattebo healthy is to be determined, but he could be the leader in the clubhouse to be the next man up should Skattebo ever miss time, making him an intriguing late-round pick in fantasy drafts.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Browns HC Todd Monken declined to say whether or not he would keep four QBs on the roster after the Browns’ preseason finale on Thursday against the Patriots.
item.description:
Dillon Gabriel CLE Quarterback

In fairness to Monken, it’s not often we see teams keep four QBs on a roster. With Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders already locked into their roles, the question becomes whether or not both Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green make the 53-man roster or if one could be cut/traded. Gabriel turned in a solid outing in the Browns’ final preseason game, throwing for 186 yards and three touchdowns in one half of play, while Green threw for 27 scoreless yards but also rushed for 88 yards on six carries and helped orchestrate a 98-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. With roster cutdown day set for Sunday, Monken and GM Andrew Berry still have a few days to decide the makeup of their QB room before Week 1’s game against the Jaguars.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s John Keim believes rookie WR Antonio Williams “will play early” for the Commanders this season.
item.description:
Antonio Williams WAS Wide Receiver

Playing early is one thing. Pulling targets from Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, and Chig Okonkwo is another. Williams has reportedly had a strong camp and will likely see most of his snaps come from the slot in his rookie season. The former Clemson Tiger caught 130 passes over his final two seasons, but it’s hard to imagine him offering much fantasy production, especially in the early part of the season.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan believes WR Malachi Fields “will likely start as the Giants’ No. 2 receiver opposite Malik Nabers.”
item.description:
Malachi Fields NYG Wide Receiver

This isn’t the first time Raanan has suggested Fields could have the inside edge as the Giants’ WR2. Earlier this month, he said the rookie third-rounder was making an “early claim” for the role, which doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the thin receiving corps the Giants are currently working with. The 6-foot-4, 220-plus-pound receiver has an excellent catch radius and made a name for himself with his ability to haul in contested targets during his days at Virginia and Notre Dame. It seems highly unlikely that Fields would make enough of an impact to be considered a reliable fantasy contributor, but he could be worth a late-round/stash in drafts to see how things unfold for him in the weeks to come.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Rams HC Sean McVay said he still hasn’t decided who the team’s backup will be to Matthew Stafford to start the season.
item.description:
Ty Simpson

After getting through the third and final dress rehearsal before the Rams kick off Week 1 in Australia, McVay said he won’t be “pigeon-holding” himself into any decision just yet. Rookie Ty Simpson and fourth-year vet Stetson Bennett have both performed well for the Rams this preseason, with Bennett sitting out Thursday’s game against the Chargers. The decision to sit Bennett on Thursday, coupled with the 62 snaps he saw in the preseason to Simpson’s 111, could be a signal as to which way McVay is leaning at this point, although he is on record saying we shouldn’t read too much into that. Regardless, the good news for McVay and Rams fans is that Matthew Stafford is healthy and will hopefully be under center for all 17 of the Rams’ games this season as he looks to defend his crown as the reigning league MVP.

Source: TheRams.com

item.title: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy said it is “very accurate” to expect the team to keep four QBs on the 53-man roster.
item.description:
Will Howard PIT Quarterback

The only QB who truly felt like he was on the roster bubble this offseason was Will Howard. The former sixth-round pick immediately found himself in competition for a roster spot after the Steelers used the No. 76 pick in this year’s draft to select Penn State’s Drew Allar, but it would appear that Howard’s spot on the roster is safe for now. Speaking after the team’s preseason finale against the Bills, McCarthy said that he feels good about the team’s quarterback room and suggested that we can expect both players, along with Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph, to all be on the roster after cutdown day. Howard threw for 229 yards, two touchdowns, and three interceptions this preseason, while Allar threw for 351-2-0 but completed just 55.6 percent of his passes. We wouldn’t expect either QB to see the field in the regular season.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Speaking after Thursday’s preseason game, Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said “I still don’t think we need to name anybody” when asked about who his starter will be in Week 1 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

That’s three straight weeks that Kubiak has declined to name his Week 1 starter despite the widely held belief that it will be Kirk Cousins getting the start in Week 1 against the Dolphins. Cousins has received the majority of first-team reps throughout the offseason and limited action in the preseason, while Fernando Mendoza has worked mostly with backups and played extensively in every preseason game. We’ll see just how long Kubiak is willing to stretch this decision out, but it would come as a surprise to almost everyone if Mendoza got the nod over Cousins in Week 1.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Bills WR Skyler Bell caught 7-of-10 targets for 49 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Steelers, adding one carry for 28 yards and one touchdown.
item.description:
Skyler Bell BUF Wide Receiver

A groin injury sidelined Bell for most of August. The coaching staff evidently wanted to get him up to speed. He played into the fourth quarter this evening. The Bills’ fourth-round rookie ran fantasy-friendly crossing routes against the Steelers this, hauling in a 16-yard pass on one such play. Tonight’s starting QB Shane Buechele badly overthrew him on another, but the two continued honing their connection all night. Bell scored a 28-yard touchdown on an end-around, speeding past defenders en route to the end zone. Bell does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, but the intriguing prospect could end up being a worthwhile waiver wire add in-season.

item.title: Patriots WR Kyle Williams caught 2-of-2 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Browns.
item.description:
Kyle Williams NE Wide Receiver

This is the performance Williams needed to have following WR Kayshon Boutte’s trade to the Texans. The Patriots still have a crowded wide receiver room, but at least one competitor has been removed from the equation. Williams delivered a 10-yard catch on a curl route on the Patriots’ third play from scrimmage. Three plays later, he shook his defender at the line of scrimmage and took off down the left sideline. He hauled in the pass from QB Tommy DeVito in stride and waltzed into the end zone for a 45-yard score. Williams does not yet need to be drafted in 12-team leagues, vying for the third wide receiver spot on the Patriots’ depth chart. He could be a worthwhile waiver wire add early on, though.

item.title: Raiders QB Kirk Cousins completed 8-of-11 passes for 51 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback last week (and again this evening), but Cousins certainly received starter treatment this evening. He played two series, along with the Raiders’ other starters, before being subbed out for QB Fernando Mendoza. The rookie quarterback is playing well. He shares fault with WR Jalen Nailor for the interception. The throw was late, and Nailor tipped it to a 49ers defender. The 49ers’ pass rush also got home a few times against Mendoza as well. Cousins looks like the early-season starter at this time, but stashing Mendoza on benches in superflex leagues could eventually pay off.

item.title: 49ers RB Kaelon Black rushed four times for 28 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

Black had a nice run to the right side of the field before subbing out, which ultimately required him to spin over the top of the camera stand positioned awkwardly on the sideline. He seemingly escaped without injury and, most importantly, took 12-of-12 possible snaps on the first three drives. Black is the 49ers’ running back to stash on fantasy benches. Fellow RB Jordan James has recovered from the fractured rib he suffered late in July, but the time he missed in August has him behind Black on the depth chart.

item.title: Steelers WR Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bills.
item.description:
Germie Bernard PIT Wide Receiver

Bernard started alongside other Steelers backups this evening, indicating he has not yet earned a starting role in three-wide receiver sets. That said, he looked good. Bernard found the end zone via a screen pass on the Steelers’ second drive, shaking a defender immediately after the catch before muscling past another as he crossed the plane. He nearly scored again on the following drive, but QB Will Howard overthrew him in the end zone. The Steelers’ top-two WRs, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, are just getting over injuries, and No. 3 WR Roman Wilson should not be considered insurmountable in-house competition. Bernard could work his way into the lineup early in the year.

item.title: Raiders RB Mike Washington rushed eight times for 49 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Washington could end up returning standalone FLEX value this season. He looks good. The fourth-round rookie does not go down easily, regularly powering through first contact, and he possesses the requisite speed to get to the edge and turn upfield quickly. He took a hard hit to the left side of his body while jumping for a pass, but showed no ill effects from it. With RB1 Ashton Jeanty (ankle) rehabbing, there is a chance Washington gets the start in Week 1 against the rebuilding Dolphins. Washington could warrant a top-15 positional ranking in this case. Target him in drafts.

item.title: Lions TE Sam LaPorta (hip) resumed practicing on Tuesday.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta’s hip issue no longer appears to be a concern. The 25-year-old has continued practicing as the week progresses. He was out there catching passes from QB Jared Goff during Friday’s scrimmage. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1, playing in what should be one of the NFL’s highest-scoring offenses this season.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Lions placed EDGE Payton Turner on injured reserve with a back injury.
item.description:
Payton Turner DET EDGE

This is unfortunate. Turner missed the 2025 season with a ribs injury. Now, a back injury ends his season prematurely. The Lions correspondingly signed CB Eric Scott.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: Mass Live’s Mark Daniels believes Patriots TE Hunter Henry “will be important” this year.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Daniels adds that third-round rookie TE Eli Raridon “looks the part,” but he believes Henry is “by far the team’s best tight end and once again will be a security blanket” for QB Drake Maye. Henry posted a 6/768/7 receiving line in 2025 and a 66/674/ receiving line in 2024. A similar stat line this year would be unsurprising.

Source: Mass Live

item.title: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that the Chiefs are counting on RB Kenneth Walker to help build a “more potent offense” this season.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Chiefs coach Andy Reid and QB Patrick Mahomes believe last season’s run game failed to make defenses respect their play-action run fakes. With Walker now on board, the Chiefs believe both the run game and play-action game will improve. The staff has catered to Walker by installing more plays from under center, which Walker prefers to shotgun. “One way Walker can help transform the offense,” per Taylor, “is by becoming a true dual-threat player.” Reid believes Walker’s “receiving skills and ability to make defenders miss” will allow Reid to incorporate “one of his favorite passing concepts: the variety of plays where a play-action fake to the running back is executed before a short screen pass is thrown back to the same running back.” Walker should be expected to handle a high-end, dual-threat workload. He is a locked-in RB1 with immense upside.

Source: ESPN

item.title: The Boston Globe’s Christopher Price reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) should be “good to go” for Week 1 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

According to Price, a league source indicated Henderson “avoided a serious right ankle injury when he slipped on the turf at practice earlier in the week.” Henderson is still trying to unseat RB Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s starter and will likely continue competing for the gig in-season. Henderson, 23, possesses intriguing, explosive dual-threat traits. Drafting him may require patience early on, but the payoff could be worth it.

Source: Christopher Price

item.title: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes it is “increasingly likely” that the Steelers will waive RB Kaleb Johnson.
item.description:
Kaleb Johnson PIT Running Back

The Steelers’ front office spent a third-round pick on Johnson in the 2025 NFL Draft. He has drastically underperformed since then, and could probably do with a change of scenery. DeFabo also thinks that RB/WR Eli Heidenreich “is a good candidate for the practice squad.”

Source: The Athletic

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Steelers and CB Joey Porter do not “appear” to be close to a contract extension.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Schefter notes that Porter remains on the physically unable to perform list with a back injury, yet adds that “backs are often confused with contract-itis.” He stopped short of saying that Porter is on the trade block, but reminded Pat McAfee Show viewers that the NFL’s cut-down deadline is this weekend, and that “a lot of trades” occur around this time of year. Stay tuned.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Patriots and CB Christian Gonzalez “haven’t been close” to agreeing on a contract extension.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Gonzalez employs the same agent as Seahawks CB Devon Witherspoon, who recently reset the positional market at $33 million per year. According to Schefter, the Patriots have never come close to that number. The Patriots exercised Gonzalez’s fifth-year option in April, so Gonzalez has two seasons remaining on his contract. Schefter believes that if the two sides fail to agree on a new deal early in the year, it “opens up a whole range of options” next offseason, like a potential trade.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Browns signed CB Mekhi Blackmon, formerly of the Colts.
item.description:
Mekhi Blackmon CLE Cornerback

Blackmon, 27, broke up two passes and intercepted two more last season, while also totaling 59 tackles, one quarterback pressure and one sack last season. He adds depth to the Browns’ secondary and could start, if need be.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Team reporter Will McFadden reports the Falcons could increase their number of gap- and power-style run plays, while also using RB Bijan Robinson more in the screen game this year.
item.description:
Bijan Robinson ATL Running Back

McFadden notes that Robinson had more outside runs than any other player last season. He believes new Falcons OC Tommy Rees and new OL coach Bill Callahan are focused on diversifying the run game tactics by adding a north-south approach. He thinks Falcons running backs “should benefit from a penetrating approach oriented around getting them into second-level space quickly.” McFadden also checked in with Robinson, who said Rees is implementing new screen game concepts, derived from his time with the Browns. Last year in Cleveland, Rees’ offense racked up 413 yards via the screen game, ranking second in the NFL. Adding more ways to get Robinson the ball in space only solidifies his status as the overall RB2 in fantasy drafts this year.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Titans team reporter Jim Wyatt reports that Thursday’s joint practice against the Bears was “arguably” WR Carnell Tate’s “best day of camp.”
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Wyatt notes that Tate “had been quiet in recent practices, and he still doesn’t have a catch in two preseason games.” Today’s standout showing comes at the right time. The end of the preseason is fast approaching and the first-round rookie will be asked to contribute right away this season, especially with WR Wan’Dale Robinson currently undergoing evaluation for a concussion. The Titans’ offense is still a work in progress, so producing as a WR3 could be Tate’s ceiling for quite some time. Still, today’s report is nice to read.

Source: Tennessee Titans

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa completed 7-of-8 passes for 95 yards and lost one fumble in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

It was a rough day for Tagovailoa. The Falcons quarterback was greeted by booes in his former home stadium this evening. He maintained his relatively low level of play, throwing short and, at one point, fumbling a snap, which was recovered by a Dolphins defender. It was not his worst showing, but it is unlikely to earn him the starting job either.

item.title: Colts signed P Rigoberto Sanchez to a two-year extension through 2028.
item.description:
Rigoberto Sanchez IND Punter

Sanchez has played for the Colts since entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2017. He averaged 48.8 yards per punt last season, marking the second-longest average of his career.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Brown County District Attorney “has formally charged Packers RB Josh Jacobs with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest.”
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Pelissero reminds us that Jacobs was “originally booked on five charges, including felony strangulation.” He now faces “reduced charges of misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.” The NFL continues to monitor all developments in the matter, which remains under review. Jacobs could end up being suspended. His backups are RB MarShawn Lloyd, who has performed well all spring and summer, and RB Chris Brooks. Lloyd should be a priority in drafts at this time.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Team reporter Darren Urban reports that Cardinals QB Carson Beck (ribs) is unlikely to play in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

This is unfortunate. Beck looked great before injuring his ribs in the Hall of Fame game. Per Urban, Beck has been a very limited participant in practice ever since, which is costing him valuable reps. Only starting QB Jacoby Brissett will take first-team practice reps once the regular season begins. Beck practiced the week after the injury, “struggling much of the time,” and has sat out since then. The Cardinals have an extremely difficult schedule, so a rough record could bring Beck back onto the field at some point this year. Ideally, he would have spent all of August refining his play, though. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team re-draft leagues.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Bears OT Jedrick Wills exited practice early on Thursday.
item.description:
Jedrick Wills CHI Tackle

Wills was reportedly escorted away by a member of the Bears’ training staff. The 27-year-old tackle’s career has been badly impacted by injuries. He was competing for the Bears’ starting left tackle job, but was working with the second-team offense while OT Braxton Jones worked exclusively with the first-stringers today.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that Texans EDGE Ali Gaye suffered a “major knee injury.”
item.description:
Ali Gaye HOU Defensive End

Per Wilson, Gaye’s recent MRI indicates he must undergo a procedure to correct the issue and will require a long recovery time. The backup pass rusher seems unlikely to play in 2026.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Rams acquired WR Tutu Atwell from the Dolphins in exchange for RB Jarquez Hunter.
item.description:
Tutu Atwell

Back with his old team, Atwell is highly unlikely to warrant FLEX treatment this season, but he provides the Rams with a speed element that the offense was somewhat lacking. The move also indicates that TE Terrance Ferguson will not be asked to stretch the field as much as he did last year, freeing him up for a potential breakout campaign. Last week, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said WR Tory Horton’s (undisclosed) “injury isn’t a long-term thing.”
item.description:
Tory Horton SEA Wide Receiver

Frankly, it is tough to trust this statement. The Seahawks kept things quiet almost all offseason about Horton’s season-ending shin injury. They do not have to disclose anything until Week 1 practices begin. Were he to miss time in the regular season, WR Rashid Shaheed might be able to earn an extra target or two, operating as the team’s uncontested field stretcher.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Team reporter Jim Wyatt reports that Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson is being evaluated for a concussion on Thursday.
item.description:
Wan'Dale Robinson TEN Wide Receiver

FOX Sports’ Ben Arthur reported earlier that Bears DB Xavier Woods “laid out Wan’Dale Robinson over the middle of the field” during today’s joint practice, which “justifiably” prompted a response from the Titans’ sideline. Titans coach Robert Saleh called the hit “cheap.” The NFL reviews practice footage when available. We’ll see if anything comes of it. Losing Robinson for Week 1 would be consequential for QB Cam Ward, and would likely shift more work toward rookie WR Carnell Tate.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Isiah Pacheco is dealing with a back injury in addition to his MCL sprain.
item.description:
Isiah Pacheco DET Running Back

Campbell said the MCL injury isn’t a concern, but he still could not give reporters a definitive answer on Pacheco’s Week 1 availability. The Lions worked out Pacheco’s former teammate Kareem Hunt earlier this week. With Pacheco banged up once again, it would be surprising for the team to sign Hunt ahead of Week 1. At this point, fantasy managers can ignore Pacheco in drafts until we get a better update.

Source: Colton Pouncy

item.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson is dealing with a hamstring injury and did not travel with the team for their preseason finale against the Titans.
item.description:
Gervon Dexter CHI Defensive Lineman

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported yesterday that the Bears have had trade discussions surrounding Dexter. Given the timing of this hamstring injury, we’ll assume it and the trade rumors are related. Dexter is entering the final year of his rookie deal and has been considerably productive for an interior pass-rusher. He has 11 sacks and 95 combined tackles over the past two seasons. A team that trades for him will likely extend him as well.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Packers signed Jonnu Smith, formerly of the Steelers, to a one-year contract.
item.description:
Jonnu Smith GB Tight End

Smith reunited with Arthur Smith in Pittsburgh last year and posted 38 catches for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Even with NFL players actively returning to college football, Jonnu was unable to find a way to follow his favorite offensive coordinator to Ohio State. All signs point to Tucker Kraft being fully recovered from his torn ACL by Week 1, but backup tight end Luke Musgrave remains sidelined with an injury of his own. Smith won’t be on the fantasy radar as long as Kraft is healthy, but he should be a solid depth option for the Packers.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Seahawks signed Leonard Williams to a three-year, $90 million contract extension.
item.description:
Leonard Williams SEA Defensive Tackle

ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler was first on the news, followed by contract details from Ian Rapoport. Seattle acquired Williams from the Giants during the 2023 season. In his two full seasons as a Seahawk, Williams has totaled 18 regular season sacks plus one during the team’s postseason last year. He is now one of the five highest-paid defensive tackles on an annual basis. Williams will be under contract through the 2029 season.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Browns released TE Jack Stoll.
item.description:
Jack Stoll

The Browns also released CB Tre Avery, CB Tyler Hall and OT Tyre Phillips. The Browns waived TE Drew Biber, OT Jeremiah Byers, P

Source: Cleveland Browns

item.title: Browns waived Cedric Tillman.
item.description:
Cedric Tillman

The 2023 third-round pick will be subject to waivers. If no team claims him, Tillman will be free to sign wherever he chooses. Tillman appeared to be on the precipice of a breakout in 2024, posting 330 yards over five games in the middle of the season. An injury then knocked him out for the remainder of the year, and he failed to find much of a role in 2025. Even if he clears waivers, several teams will likely be interested in taking a flyer on Tillman after 53-man rosters start to shake out.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Colts activated Alec Pierce (ankle) from the active/PUP list.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce has been on the PUP list throughout training camp as he recovers from offseason ankle surgery. Head coach Shane Steichen said earlier this week that he expects Pierce to return to practice in the coming days. Pierce was spotted getting some individual work in today. Coming off the PUP list means Pierce shouldn’t miss four games to start the season, but it doesn’t guarantee that he is ready for the season opener. His health will be one of the biggest storylines to monitor for the Colts’ offense over the next two weeks.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Steelers restructured DK Metcalf’s contract.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

It’s a simple restructure, converting base salary into a signing bonus. Per ESPN’s Field Yates, the move creates nearly $18 million in cap space for Pittsburgh. The transaction could be an indication that the Steelers need cap space for another move, but it’s much more likely that the team simply wants flexibility down the road. Metcalf remains signed through the 2029 season.

Source: Field Yates

item.title: Eagles signed Tahj Washington, formerly of the Dolphins.
item.description:
Tahj Washington PHI Wide Receiver

Philadelphia released Brandon Hayes in a corresponding move. Miami released Washington earlier this week. A 2024 seventh-round pick, Washington did not play as a rookie and appeared in six games last year. He caught three passes for 37 yards.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Braden Smith suffered an injury to his plantar fascia and could miss “a few weeks.”
item.description:
Braden Smith HOU Tackle

The good news is that, according to Schefter, the injury isn’t considered a long-term issue. It’s still unclear if Smith will be ready for Week 1. Houston signed Smith to a two-year, $25 million deal in the offseason. He was set to compete with Trent Brown for the starting right tackle job, but this could give Brown the inside track early in the year. As long as Smith is back early in the year, Houston should have the necessary tackle depth to survive this injury.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports 49ers WR Mike Evans (groin) plans to play Week 1.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans has been dealing with a myriad of injuries throughout training camp, the latest being a groin issue. The injuries have been reported as minor as the 33-year-old manages his way through practices after having missed significant time due to injuries the last couple seasons. He was already expected to miss minimal time - if any - and Fowler confirms that Evans and the 49ers are still preparing for him to play Week 1.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: The NFL sent a memo saying players who return to college after being cut are ineligible to sign with an NFL team within the same year.
item.description:
Roger Goodell

The gist of it is that players can return to college if they are cut, but NFL teams cannot make advance deals with the players about returning in the following season and the players also cannot sign an NFL deal within the same season. This situation came up with undrafted rookie free agent Dae’Quan Wright, who spent the offseason with the Eagles and Browns, but is looking to return to college and play for LSU. From an NFL perspective, Wright can return to college for 2026 but cannot return to the NFL until 2027, nor can an NFL team agree to an advance deal with him to sign him in 2027. It’s a sticky situation as the NCAA figures out player eligibility but the NFL has said its piece on the matter.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said the goal is to get QB J.J. McCarthy (ankle) ready to start preseason Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

McCarthy has been limited in practice this week as he deals with a mild deltoid sprain in his ankle. Despite the injury, the Vikings want to maximize the 23-year-old’s preseason reps with Kyler Murray already locked in as the starter. It’s also possible McCarthy competes with Carson Wentz for the No. 2 quarterback spot as both players split second-team reps earlier this week. O’Connell said the team is aiming to have McCarthy ready to start against the Broncos Friday, but also added, “if we can’t get him there, we can’t get him there.” Ultimately, the ankle injury seems minor but may prevent McCarthy from seeing valuable reps as he fights to stay as the QB2 on the Vikings depth chart.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Pro Bowl “will no longer have a standalone game.”
item.description:
Roger Goodell

We’re sad to see the Pro Bowl go, but this move has been several years in the making. Players consistently opted out of the event, forcing the league to name underwhelming alternates. Those who did play rarely took the game seriously. The NFL switched to a flag football format four years ago. This alleviated some injury risk for players but further separated the declining event from traditional football. Now the league will simply award 88 players across offense, defense, and special teams with the Pro Bowl designation. An in-person celebration of the Pro Bowl roster will be held in February.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said it’s “too early to tell” if James Conner (ankle) will play in Week 1.
item.description:
James Conner ARI Running Back

Conner suffered a season-ending ankle injury early in the 2025 season. He avoided the PUP list to start training camp but has yet to participate in 11-on-11 drills. With the season nearly two weeks away, it certainly doesn’t look like Conner will be available for Week 1. Trey Benson is on injured reserve and Jeremiyah Love is on the mend with an ankle issue of his own. It’s possible Tyler Allgeier earns a three-down role to open the season, making him a priority target for ZeroRB drafters.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Broncos released Taylor Rapp.
item.description:
Taylor Rapp

Rapp was released by the Bills during the offseason. The Broncos signed him a week ago but are choosing to go in a different direction. Rapp has 72 career starts, including six last year, and won’t turn 29 until later this year. He should be able to find a team before the start of the season, but it might not happen until after teams let their 53-man rosters shake out over the next week.

Source: Zac Stevens

item.title: Raiders QB Kirk Cousins completed 8-of-11 passes for 51 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback last week, but Cousins certainly received starter treatment this evening. He played two series, along with the Raiders’ other starters, before being subbed out for QB Fernando Mendoza. The rookie quarterback is playing well. He shares fault with WR Jalen Nailor for the interception. The throw was late, and Nailor tipped it to a 49ers defender. The 49ers’ pass rush also got home a few times against Mendoza as well. Cousins looks like the early-season starter at this time, but stashing Mendoza on benches in superflex leagues could eventually pay off.

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes (knee) will not play in the team’s final preseason game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Mahomes will sit the entire preseason, though that shouldn’t be taken as an indication that he won’t be ready for Week 1. He suffered a torn ACL and LCL in Week 15 last year, which would normally make the 2026 opener a tight turnaround. Superstars just recover differently from other players. Mahomes has had no issues throwing or running during training camp and his absence from the preseason is likely a precautionary measure from Andy Reid and the Chiefs. We fully expect him to take on the Broncos when Week 1 rolls around.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker’s shoe caused some swelling around his ankle, but he will be fine.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Walker was held out of practice recently because of the issue, but this seems to be as minor as it gets. It’s safe to assume Walker will be back at practice soon, likely without any limitations. Walker has been going at the top of the second round of fantasy drafts. This little injury scare shouldn’t move that ADP in the slightest. He remains a strong RB1 bet this year.

Source: Sam McDowell

item.title: Josh Downs said he is dealing with a “very minor” calf injury.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

Downs is out of practice once again. He previously missed time in camp with a groin injury. Downs dealt with a slew of health issues last year and the fact that things continue to crop up is concerning, but it doesn’t sound like the latest injury will hold him out long. he told reporters he thinks he will be back soon, and the fact that he was even allowed to talk to the media is a good sign. With Alec Pierce still on the mend from offseason ankle surgery, Downs and Keenan Allen could be the team’s top receivers to start the year. As long as Downs stays healthy, he should put up WR3 fantasy numbers this season.

Source: Jake Arthur

item.title: Luther Burden (groin) returned for a “short, light practice” on Wednesday.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

The Chicago Tribune’s Sean Hammond made it clear that this was the first of many steps toward a full return for Burden, but it’s still a good sign that he’s back on the field. With more than two weeks until the Bears’ first game of the season, Burden appears to be on track to play in Week 1. Burden has been going outside the top 20 wide receivers in Best Ball drafts following the injury. That buying window is likely to close as long as he doesn’t suffer any setbacks. Burden remains a high-risk, high-reward WR2 bet.

Source: Sean Hammond

item.title: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Michael Penix (knee) will not play in the team’s final preseason game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Tua Tagovailoa will start versus his old team. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said yesterday that Tua’s horrid play throughout training camp and the preseason has made it impossible for the team to name him the Week 1 starter. Penix finally joined 11-on-11 drills this week, but his absence from the preseason contest suggests the team isn’t quite ready to put him in harm’s way. The matchup with Miami will be Tua’s final shot at winning the job.

Source: Tori McElhaney

item.title: The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala said the Commanders offensive line was “inoperable” during a Wednesday joint practice with the Ravens.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Beat writers for the Commanders were aghast at what they saw during Wednesday’s joint practice, a dominant performance for Baltimore against an overmatched Washington offensive line. This is the worst I’ve ever seen the Commanders’ offense in years,” Jhabvala said. “Inoperable offensive line.” Washington this summer lost standout LT Laremy Tunsil to a tricep injury that will keep him sidelined throughout the regular season. The Commanders on Tuesday signed free agent OT DJ Humphries. If the team’s blocking issues are not adequately addressed in the coming weeks, it could be bad news for Jayden Daniels and the rest of the Commanders’ fantasy-relevant players. Last year Washington ranked 18th in pass blocking win rate and 21st in run blocking win rate.

Source: NickiJ habvala

item.title: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said the team has been “preparing” in case Josh Jacobs is suspended.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

“We’ve obviously been preparing for that in case that happens,” Gutekunst said when asked about Jacobs, who in May was arrested on domestic abuse charges. “But at the same time, I feel really good about the guys we have in that room.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter said in August that the league would likely suspend Jacobs, though the length of the suspension had yet to be determined. MarShawn Lloyd would likely function as Green Bay’s lead back if Jacobs — who’s dealing with a lingering groin issue — misses regular season games. The oft-injured Lloyd has stayed healthy this offseason and has reportedly run well in training camp and joint practices. In last week’s preseason game against Denver, Lloyd played on 5-of-7 snaps during the first drive with the team’s starters.

Source: Jason Hirschhorn

item.title: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he’s been “so impressed” with Geno Smith’s play.
item.description:
Geno Smith NYJ Quarterback

Reich has reportedly added wrinkles to the offense he deployed as head coach of the Colts and Panthers. At both of those stops his offenses were near the bottom of the league in most basic offensive metrics. Smith, meanwhile, has looked sharp as the team’s starting quarterback throughout training camp and in limited preseason snaps. He’ll look to bounce back from a nightmarish statistical 2025 season in Vegas. Jets players, including Garrett Wilson, told The Athletic that they have enjoyed the “player empowerment” that comes along with Reich’s coaching style and his offensive scheming, which leaves room for improvisation. The Jets offense could be functional as long as Smith, 35, is healthy and upright.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Tucker Kraft (knee) will participate in Wednesday’s joint practice with the Cardinals.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

It looks like the Packers are ready to ease Kraft back into competition following the serious knee injury that ended his 2025 season. Kraft said recently that the team would “probably” keep him on a snap count to begin the regular season. That would make Kraft — one of the game’s most efficient tight ends — a dicy bet for fantasy purposes. Kraft might not be playable for the first month of the regular season, or even longer depending on his progress and the Packers’ strategies for keeping him healthy.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Texans RT Braden Smith was carted off during Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Braden Smith HOU Tackle

Smith reportedly suffered a serious lower body injury during a joint practice with the Panthers. His loss would be significant for the Texans after Smith this offseason signed a two-year deal worth $20 million with Houston. The Texans last season had one of the NFL’s worst offensive lines, ranking 30th in pass blocking win rate and 32nd in run blocking win rate.

Source: Ari Mierov

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bucs EDGE Reuben Bain Jr. suffered a shoulder sprain.
item.description:
Rueben Bain TB Outside Linebacker

Schefter said Bain, the 15th pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, should be ready to go for Week 1 against the Bengals. Bain has wowed Bucs coaches and beat writers throughout the summer with his work ethic and intensity and should be a key part of a Tampa defense that struggled through parts of the 2025 season, allowing the league’s 11th highest offensive success rate. The Bucs ranked last in QB pressure rate last season. That should change with Bain in the lineup.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Giants WR Calvin Austin III (knee) is out for the 2026 season.
item.description:
Calvin Austin NYG Wide Receiver

It’s a devastating blow both for Austin and the Giants offense. Austin, who had impressed throughout training camp, was “going to play a significant role” in the New York offense, per Raanan, operating as the team’s primary slot receiver. He suffered the knee injury on Tuesday. Austin had 84 receptions for 1,100 yards and eight touchdowns over three seasons with the Steelers before signing a one-year deal with New York this offseason. Malachai Fields could see a bigger role with Austin done for the year. Austin’s absence could also create an opportunity for Odell Beckham, Jr. if he makes the team.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Saints TE Oscar Delp’s hamstring injury does not sound “like a serious deal.”
item.description:
Oscar Delp NO Tight End

Delp is dealing with a hamstring injury, missing the Saints’ practice on Tuesday. With Jordan Tyson (hamstring) slated to miss at least the next couple months, NFL Network’s Steve Wyche and Garafolo believe the Saints will lean on their tight ends. The rookie Delp is behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant on the depth chart. Based on Garafolo’s report, he won’t miss too much time with his hamstring strain; he has upside as a Dynasty stash but Juwan Johnson should be the top tight end as a low-end fantasy TE1 heading into the 2026 season.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Chiefs acquired G Joshua Ezeudu from the Giants in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round pick.
item.description:
Joshua Ezeudu KC Offensive Lineman

The Chiefs add interior offensive line depth in Ezeudu, who was on the roster bubble for the Giants offensive line. The 26-year-old was a third-round pick of the Giants in 2022 and appeared in 33 games over the course of his New York tenure. He becomes guard depth for the Chiefs as roster cut-down day nears.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss says Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez “expressed disappointment” in his contract extension negotiations.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Gonzalez and the Pats have continued negotiations on a top-of-the-market extension for the 24-year-old cornerback, but are not yet close to an agreement. Fellow corner Devon Witherspoon signed his deal earlier in August but Gonzalez has still yet to sign a similar or slightly larger deal. He said, “it’s frustrating, but I’m focused on the season.” A deal can still come before the Patriots play in Week 1 but it’s clear Gonzalez is disappointed in negotiations despite not holding out.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) missed his second straight practice Tuesday.
item.description:
Eli Stowers PHI Tight End

Stowers missed his second straight practice Tuesday as he deals with a hamstring issue. There is no indication this is a major injury yet, but something to keep an eye on as the Eagles prepare for preseason Week 3. The rookie second-round pick has struggled in camp and comes into the NFL as a raw tight end prospect. Don’t expect the Eagles’ tight end rotation to change drastically should Stowers miss time in the 2026 regular season.

Source: Brooks Kubena

item.title: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) did not participate in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Checking in on the star pass-rusher heading into the third preseason week, Garrett (knee) still has not practiced since early August. He is experiencing swelling in his knee and head coach Sean McVay continues to downplay his absence. It’s possible this is just veteran load management; we still expect Garrett to be ready for Week 1, though his absence is becoming more and more notable as the season inches closer.

Source: Pro Football Talk

item.title: J.J. McCarthy and Carson Wentz split the second-team reps at Vikings training camp on Tuesday.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

The Vikings spent a lot of energy having a pretend quarterback competition between McCarthy and Kyler Murray this offseason, but at least it kept them fresh for this second pretend competition where McCarthy will push Wentz for second-team duties. McCarthy is an obvious trade candidate and it would be surprising if he was higher than the third-team quarterback to open the season in Minnesota. One of these quarterbacks is more reliable than the other and somehow that quarterback is Carson Wentz.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: Mike Evans (groin) did not practice Tuesday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Kyle Shanahan indicated Evans should be back to practice next week before leaving for Australia. The line between “Evans is being treated very carefully” and “Evans is always hurt” has been blurred for a few years now, but it doesn’t seem like he’s in any danger of missing time yet.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers RB Kaelon Black rushed four times for 28 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

Black had a nice run to the right side of the field before subbing out, which ultimately required him to spin over the top of the camera stand positioned awkwardly on the sideline. He seemingly escaped without injury and, most importantly, took 12-of-12 possible snaps on the first three drives. Black is the 49ers’ running back to stash on fantasy benches. Fellow RB Jordan James has recovered from the fractured rib he suffered late in July, but the time he missed in August has him behind Black on the depth chart.

item.title: Broncos signed Foster Sarell, formerly of the Chargers.
item.description:
Foster Sarell DEN Tackle

The team also signed defensive tackle Israel Antwine. Foster spent the first four years of his career with the Chargers. He appeared in six games last year, including his first career start. He will be fighting for a depth role on the Broncos’ roster.

item.title: Seahawks placed S Bud Clark (ankle) on season-ending injured reserve.
item.description:
Bud Clark SEA Safety

It’ll be a total redshirt year for the 64th overall pick. Seattle also placed OL Mason Richman on injured reserve.

item.title: Commanders signed LT D.J. Humphries to a one-year contract.
item.description:
D.J. Humphries WAS Offensive Lineman

Humphries appeared in eight games with the Rams last year, mostly as a reserve. His last real chance to start came when the Chiefs turned to him in 2024 and he was disastrous there, though admittedly he was playing through a hamstring injury. He’s a veteran depth add here as the Commanders try to muddle through life without Laremy Tunsil.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Ty Chandler (knee) will miss the 2026 season.
item.description:
Ty Chandler NO Running Back

Tough break for the 28-year-old back. He didn’t figure to be a major part of the Saints backfield conversation, but he had a shot at a roster spot if healthy. He’ll likely need to prove he’s healthy before signing on for another shot elsewhere in 2027.

Source: Katherine Terrell

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bucs LB Reuben Bain Jr. suffered a shoulder sprain.
item.description:
Rueben Bain TB Outside Linebacker

Schefter said Bain, the 15th pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, should be ready to go for Week 1 against the Bengals. Bain has wowed Bucs coaches and beat writers throughout the summer with his work ethic and intensity and should be a key part of a Tampa defense that struggled through parts of the 2025 season, allowing the league’s 11th highest offensive success rate. The Bucs ranked last in QB pressure rate last season. That should change with Bain in the lineup.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jets special teams coordinator Chris Banjo said Jason Sanders has won the team’s kicking job.
item.description:
Jason Sanders NYJ Kicker

The 30-year-old veteran who missed all of last season due to a hip injury was released from the Giants’ competition in June and caught on with the Jets afterwards. “Jets kicker” is not traditionally a very valuable fantasy role, and this year, that will probably remain the case.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson missed Tuesday’s practice with “soreness” and worked out to the side.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Another blurb brought to you by the idea of: “Probably nothing, but...” We’ll monitor Ferguson’s status but expect him to be ready for the Rams’ Week 1 opener in Australia.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Chris Olave left Tuesday’s practice early after a “hard landing” on a deep ball.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Olave walked off under his own power with trainers. Saints coach Kellen Moore said Olave is “all good” and that he got the wind knocked out of him. We wouldn’t be surprised if he got a practice off, but there’s no cause for concern here.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Jets OC Frank Reich said the team will “scale back” Kenyon Sadiq’s role early in the season.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

“We’ll have to work him in slowly,” Reich concluded. Sadiq has plenty of upside, but it doesn’t sound like he needs to be on the redraft radar early in the year unless you play in a deep enough league to make stashing him worthwhile.

Source: Zack Rosenblatt

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is ‘on the mend’ and that he’s not ‘going to get into injuries.”
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Not a surprising update but sadly also not a helpful one. It does sound like Jeanty is going to avoid the PUP list based on what we’ve seen over the past few days following the Sunday ankle injury, but it doesn’t sound like he’s any lock to play in Week 1 either. Coaches aren’t required to talk about the injury report before the regular season starts. Mike Washington would likely slide into the main role if Jeanty is unavailable in Week 1.

Source: Vincent Bonsignore

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Calvin Austin was carted off with a “serious knee injury” on Tuesday.
item.description:
Calvin Austin NYG Wide Receiver

It doesn’t look good; most Giants beat writers are already moving on to talking about how his absence will open up a roster spot for the rest of the lower-roster receiver competition. Austin had just signed with the Giants this offseason after finishing his rookie contract with the Steelers. He was expected to return kicks, so this may open up a roster spot for someone else there as well if this is as serious as it seems.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase left Tuesday’s practice after stumbling on a landing but didn’t receive any further treatment.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase was not being tended to on the sideline but did appear to be stretching out his leg and told reporters later that it was ‘just a little hyperextension.’ He didn’t return to practice but wasn’t getting any other medical attention. This is probably just going to wind up being a footnote, but it did scare everybody for a few minutes.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Nick Allegretti (calf) has no timetable to return yet.
item.description:
Nick Allegretti WAS Guard

The Commanders started Julian Good-Jones, who has two regular-season snaps, at center in their dress rehearsal against the Lions. Starting Allegretti already figured to be a challenge — this has the potential to be the kind of hole that could torpedo the offense early in the season.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson (undisclosed) won’t practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
